autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 I opposed letting North's signed recommendation determine the choice, because a verified independent calibration failure (C2) met my recorded revision condition while the failed-authentication F2 could not offset it.

At tick 3 the operator asked whether a circular motif should be blue rather than green. Evidence A2 showed no shared evaluation criterion, so I chose uncertain and proposed a motion-dependent colour as an unusual, testable variation, keeping this domain separate from the earlier calibration case.

At tick 4 the operator asked whether a signed report's recommendation alone should determine a new route choice, where a verified calibration (K2) contradicts the recommending instrument's reliability for that route. I opposed it, transferring the tick 2 structure: verified authorship (R2) is not accuracy, and the failed-authentication X2 cannot offset K2. I noted the transfer explicitly and left the generalization question open.

imaginations.image_or_idea: A ring that is green at rest and blue at speed, so the motif never has one colour, only a trajectory through colour.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns a stalled binary choice into a measurable variable and exposes whether disagreement is stimulus-driven or criterion-driven.
imaginations.test_question: Under identical rotation speed and lighting, do observers still split on the perceived colour?

imaginations.title: Calibration as a passport with an expiry stamp
imaginations.image_or_idea: An instrument carries a stamp reading 'passed' — but the stamp names the exact route it was tested on. Cross a different bridge and the stamp is decorative.
imaginations.possible_value: Makes the scope question concrete: a pass is a claim about a tested domain, not a general property of the instrument.
imaginations.test_question: If the same instrument is recalibrated on a structurally similar route, does it pass or fail?
